questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: How to write the dot net server control?
questions.explanation_en: An ASP.NET server control is written as <asp:ControlType ID="..." runat="server" .../>. The runat="server" attribute tells ASP.NET to process the control on the server instead of sending it to the browser as plain HTML. 'runin', 'runas' and 'run' are not valid attributes.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following parameters is used to create a hyperlink in HTML?
questions.explanation_en: A hyperlink is made with the anchor tag and its href attribute, for example Link. href (hypertext reference) holds the destination URL. 'url', 'link' and 'path' are not attributes of the tag.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following methods is used to slide down an element?
questions.explanation_en: In jQuery, $(selector).slideDown(speed) shows a hidden element with a sliding-down animation, and slideUp()/slideToggle() are its partners. moveDown(), moveBelow() and slideBelow() are not jQuery methods.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: Which directive is used for binding the model data to the view?
questions.explanation_en: In AngularJS, ng-model binds the value of an input/select/textarea to a property on the scope (two-way data binding), so the view and the model stay in sync. ng-app starts the application, and 'ng-model-view', 'ng-model-app' and 'ng-app-model' do not exist.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: With reference to CSS, which of the following allows to change property values smoothly over a given duration?
questions.explanation_en: CSS transitions (the transition property) change a property's value smoothly over a set duration, for example transition: width 2s. Masking hides parts of an element, web fonts load custom fonts, and text effects style text. None of these animate value changes.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en:
Which of the following statements is/are true with reference to java servlets?
(i) A Servlet is a Java program that runs without a web server.
(ii) It receives the requests and responds to them using related protocols (usually HTTP).
questions.explanation_en: A servlet is a Java program that runs inside a web server or servlet container (such as Tomcat), so statement (i) is false. Statement (ii) is true: it receives client requests and sends responses, usually over HTTP. So only (ii) is correct.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following can be used for the frontend or user interface while developing a web application?
questions.explanation_en: JavaScript runs in the browser and is used with HTML and CSS to build the front end (user interface). PHP and Django (Python) are server-side back-end technologies, and SQL is used to query databases.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following is NOT a front-end design tool?
questions.explanation_en: PHP is a server-side scripting language that runs on the web server, so it is a back-end tool. AngularJS and jQuery are JavaScript front-end libraries/frameworks, and Chrome DevTools is used to inspect and debug front-end pages.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following types of XML parsers is an object that contains all the information of an XML document and is composed like a tree structure?
questions.explanation_en: A DOM (Document Object Model) parser loads the whole XML document into memory as a tree of node objects that can be navigated and changed. SAX is an event-based streaming parser that does not build a tree. DOS and SAY are not XML parsers.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following is a Microsoft ActiveX control that will sort through a data file, extrapolate the necessary information and produce that information in specified areas on the web page?
questions.explanation_en: The Tabular Data Control (TDC) is a Microsoft ActiveX control that reads a delimited text data file and binds its data to elements of a web page (data binding in DHTML). Dialog bars, control bars and dialog boxes are UI elements and do not read data files.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: ______ are a database applications' universal front end that connects to the back end via the internet.
questions.explanation_en: Web browsers act as a universal front end (thin client): through the internet they connect to a web server, which talks to the back-end database. The web server and the web application sit on the server side, not at the user's end.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: In HTML body tag, which of the following attribute indicates the colour of the hyperlinks after the mouse is clicked on it?
questions.explanation_en: In the <body> tag, LINK sets the colour of unvisited links, ALINK sets the colour of a link while it is being clicked (active), and VLINK sets the colour of links that have already been visited (after they are clicked). So VLINK is the colour after the click. HLINK is not an attribute.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following is NOT an attribute that included by the HR tag which puts a horizontal line on the page?
questions.explanation_en: The <HR> tag supports the attributes SIZE (thickness), WIDTH, ALIGN and NOSHADE (draws a solid line without shading). There is no attribute called SHADE; the real attribute is NOSHADE.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following tag of HTML language is a container for the tags that contain information about the page?
questions.explanation_en: The <head> element is a container for metadata about the page: <title>, <meta>, <link>, <style> and <script>. <title> is only one tag inside the head, and <body> holds the visible content.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following form is correct to show a 'comments' in the HTML language?
questions.explanation_en: An HTML comment is written as <!-- This is a comment -->: it starts with <!-- and ends with -->. Option 4 is this form (with spaces shown between the symbols). The other options either miss the ! at the start or wrongly put ! in the closing part.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following rule is needed to be followed while declaring the XML (Extensible Markup Language) elements name?

options.en: Name must start with a number
Name must not start with the letter xml
Name cannot contain letter, numbers and other characters

questions.explanation_en: XML naming rules: element names are case-sensitive, must start with a letter or underscore, cannot contain spaces, and must not start with the letters 'xml' (in any case), because that prefix is reserved. They can contain letters, digits, hyphens, underscores and periods, so the other options are false.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following HTML tag is used to puts a line break in the text?
questions.explanation_en: is an empty tag that inserts a line break, so the following text starts on a new line. makes text bold, and and are not standard HTML tags.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following opens the linked document in the windows full body among the target values?
questions.explanation_en: target="_top" opens the linked document in the full body of the window, breaking out of all frames. _self opens in the same frame, _blank in a new window/tab, and _parent only in the immediate parent frame.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following is the syntax to write an external CSS?
questions.explanation_en: An external stylesheet is attached in the <head> with <link rel="stylesheet" type="text/css" href="style.css">. The <style> tag is for internal CSS and has no href attribute, and <a> creates a hyperlink, not a stylesheet link.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: How to change all images to black and white (100% grey)?
questions.explanation_en: The CSS filter property with the grayscale() function converts an image to grey: img { filter: grayscale(100%); }. There is no graycolor() function, and the value must not be quoted as a string (option 4).

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following is NOT an XML Parser?
questions.explanation_en: DOM (tree-based), SAX (event-based) and JDOM (Java-oriented) are XML parsers/APIs. 'Shell' is a command interpreter, not an XML parser.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: How to write the external DTD?
questions.explanation_en: An external DTD is referenced as <!DOCTYPE root-element SYSTEM "file-name">: the root element name comes first, then the keyword SYSTEM and the DTD file path. Options 1 and 3 omit or misplace the root element, and ROOT is not a DTD keyword.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following is NOT a feature of ADO.net?
questions.explanation_en: Microsoft lists the key features of ADO.NET as interoperability (XML based), maintainability, programmability, performance and scalability. 'Reachability' is not one of them.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following is a software application that helps developers to build attractive website layouts and apps with ease?
questions.explanation_en: Front-end development tools (e.g. Bootstrap, Sass, VS Code extensions) help developers build attractive layouts and user interfaces for websites and apps. Back-end tools deal with servers and databases, and database design tools model data.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following is a valid syntax for the XML element in a DTD?
questions.explanation_en: An element is declared in a DTD as <!ELEMENT element-name category> (or (content)). <!ATTLIST ...> declares attributes and <!ENTITY ...> declares entities, so they are valid but not for elements; <#ELEMENT> is invalid syntax.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following is an action or occurrence such as a mouse click, a key press, mouse movements or any system-generated notification in ASP.NET?
questions.explanation_en: In ASP.NET, an event is an action or occurrence such as a mouse click, key press, mouse movement or a system-generated notification, which triggers an event handler. Directives give compiler instructions, validators check input, and controls are UI elements.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following front-end tools is one of the most widely used CSS extension languages across the world?
questions.explanation_en: Sass (Syntactically Awesome Style Sheets) is a widely used CSS extension language that adds variables, nesting and mixins. VS Code is an editor, Git is version control and TypeScript extends JavaScript, not CSS.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: ______ is the standard that defines how web servers and application programs communicate.
questions.explanation_en: Key doubt: the Common Gateway Interface (CGI) is the standard that defines how a web server communicates with application programs (Silberschatz, Database System Concepts), so option 3 should be correct. HTTP is the protocol between the browser (client) and the web server, not between the web server and application programs. JDBC/ODBC connect applications to databases.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: ______ reads XML documents and provides access to their content and structure.
questions.explanation_en: An XML processor (parser) reads an XML document and gives applications access to its content and structure. An XML schema only defines the allowed structure; it does not read documents.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en:
What will the output of the following code snippet be?
<script>
document.write ("Hello")
document.write ("
India")
</script>
questions.explanation_en: The second string starts with a newline character. When written into HTML, a newline is treated as whitespace and rendered as a single space, so the page shows 'Hello India'. 'HelloIndia' would appear only if there were no whitespace between the strings.

tests.description: All 30 Web Technologies questions from the 4 official DSSSB TGT CS papers, with the official answers and solutions.

tests.title: Previous Year Questions — IT Tools & Emerging Tech (DSSSB 2023–24)
tests.subject: Computer Science
tests.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
tests.category: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching Special

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: _____ is a set of interrelated components that collect (or retrieve), process, store and distribute information to support decision-making and control in an organisation.

options.en: Mini model of a processed system
Max model of a processed system

questions.explanation_en: An information system is a set of interrelated components (people, hardware, software, data, procedures) that collect, process, store and distribute information to support decision-making and control in an organisation. Information technology is only the hardware/software part of such a system, not the complete set of components. The 'mini/max model' options are not standard terms.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: DSS is a computer program application used to improve a company's _____ capabilities.
questions.explanation_en: A Decision Support System (DSS) is an interactive computer system that analyses data and models to help managers make better decisions. Its main job is to improve decision-making, not marketing, delegation or resource utilisation, even though better decisions can help those areas too.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Elasticity of demand explains the _____ of the correlation between price and quantity.
questions.explanation_en: Price elasticity of demand measures the degree (how much) quantity demanded responds to a change in price, as % change in quantity divided by % change in price. It tells the strength of the relationship, not an 'angle' or 'level'.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: According to the double entry system, every transaction will have _____ entries.
questions.explanation_en: In the double entry system every transaction affects two accounts: one is debited and the other is credited with the same amount. The option written as 'Debt and Credit' means Debit and Credit. Right and left only describe the sides of a ledger account, not the entries.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: The part of the firm's capital that is required for conducting day to day expenses is called:
questions.explanation_en: Working capital (current assets minus current liabilities) is the money a firm needs for daily operations such as wages, raw material and bills. Fixed capital is invested in long-term assets like land and machinery, so it is not used for day-to-day expenses.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following systems comprises word processing, electronic filing, electronic mail, message switching, data storage and data and voice communication?
questions.explanation_en: Office Automation Systems (OAS) help office work through word processing, electronic filing, e-mail, message switching, data storage and voice/data communication. DSS and ESS help managers make decisions, and CRM manages customer relationships.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following refers to expertise and skills acquired by a person through experience or education, the theoretical or practical understanding of a subject?
questions.explanation_en: Knowledge is the expertise and skills a person gains through experience or education, that is, the theoretical or practical understanding of a subject. Synthesis means combining ideas, and problem solving is applying knowledge. Neither is the understanding itself.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Which characteristic of business refers to ‘various components of a business system are highly interacting and interdependent’?
questions.explanation_en: Interdependence means the parts of a business system (production, finance, marketing, HR) interact closely and depend on each other, so a change in one affects the others. Complexity refers to the large number of variables involved, not to this mutual dependence.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: With reference to Management Information System, which of the following categories refers to information that is concerned with long-term policy decisions that define the objectives of a business and check how well these objectives are met?
questions.explanation_en: Strategic information is used by top management for long-term policy decisions, such as setting business objectives and checking how well they are met. Tactical information is for middle management's medium-term control, and operational information is for day-to-day work.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following is NOT a component of Management Information System?
questions.explanation_en: The components of an MIS are people, hardware, software, data (database) and procedures. 'Education procedures' is not a component of MIS. People, software and data are core components.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following is the fundamental state of business activity and involves the sale and purchase of goods and services?
questions.explanation_en: Trade, the buying and selling of goods and services, is the basic core activity of business. Industry produces goods, and supply and enterprise are broader or related ideas, not the act of sale and purchase itself.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: ‘As the stock of a commodity increases with the consumer, its marginal utility to the consumer decreases’. To which of the following laws does the given statement refer to?
questions.explanation_en: The Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility says that as a consumer gets more units of a good, the extra satisfaction (marginal utility) from each additional unit falls. The Law of Demand links price and quantity demanded, not utility from stock held.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: A fixed sum that is paid by customers for a service, typically on a monthly, quarterly or annual basis, is called ______ in electronic commerce.
questions.explanation_en: In e-commerce the subscription revenue model charges customers a fixed amount every month, quarter or year to use a service (for example Netflix). Licensing gives the right to use software, and the affiliate model earns commission on referrals.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following comes under applied mathematics?
questions.explanation_en: Operations research uses mathematical methods such as linear programming, queuing theory and simulation to make decisions better, so it is a branch of applied mathematics. Management accounting and organisation are management areas, and information processing is a computing activity.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: An individual's shared experience results in __________.

options.en: tacit knowledge, systematic knowledge and shared knowledge

questions.explanation_en: In Nonaka's SECI model, socialisation means people sharing experiences (observing, imitating, working together), and what passes between them is tacit knowledge: personal know-how that is hard to write down. Systematic (explicit) knowledge is produced by putting it into documents, not by shared experience.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Which qualitative statistic is difficult to quantify precisely?
questions.explanation_en: Value (for example customer value or the value of information) is qualitative and subjective, so it is hard to measure precisely with a number. Infrastructure and models can be described and counted more concretely.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: What is effective desire?
questions.explanation_en: In economics, effective desire means a desire backed by the ability to pay and the willingness to spend, and that is the definition of demand. Consumption is the actual use of goods, and utility is the satisfaction they give. The official key (Consumption) looks wrong; option 1, Demand, is the correct answer.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: ______ primarily deals with buying and selling, particularly on a large scale.
questions.explanation_en: Commerce covers all activities involved in buying and selling goods and services, especially on a large scale, together with aids to trade such as transport, banking and insurance. Finance deals with managing money, and distribution or supply chain are only parts of commerce.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: A particular organisation or industry's most successful solutions or problem-solving methods are called ______.
questions.explanation_en: The most successful solutions or problem-solving methods developed by an organisation or industry are called best practices (Laudon's definition in knowledge management). Knowledge management is the overall process of creating, storing and sharing knowledge, not the name for those solutions. The official key (knowledge management) looks wrong; option 4 is correct.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: According to business economics, the growth of an existing product is used to estimate the demand for a new product using:
questions.explanation_en: In Joel Dean's methods for forecasting demand for a new product, the growth curve approach estimates the new product's demand from the growth pattern of an existing, established product. The substitute approach treats the new product as a replacement for an existing one and studies that product's demand instead. The official key (substitute) looks wrong; option 1 fits the question.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en:
Match the AI Ethics with its correct description.
AI Ethics | Description
I. Data privacy | 1. It is a standard metric that measures how many users in a database share a particular attribute.
II. K-anonymity | 2. It is a trade-off between the amount of data collected and the performance of a product or service.
III. L-diversity | 3. It extends the idea by merging several sensitive attributes together.
questions.explanation_en: Data privacy involves a trade-off between how much data is collected and how well a product or service performs (I-2). K-anonymity measures how many records in a database share the same attribute values, so each person is hidden among at least k others (II-1). L-diversity extends k-anonymity by requiring diversity in the sensitive attributes of each group (III-3). So the match is I-2, II-1, III-3.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en:
Match the categories of AI with its correct description.
Categories of AI | Description
I. Artificial Narrow Intelligence | 1. Level of general and strong AI that is smarter than humans if that's possible.
II. Artificial General Intelligence | 2. Such system seems to act intelligently but they don't have any awareness of what they are doing.
III. Super Intelligence | 3. Acting like a smart human and thinking like one with a conscious.
questions.explanation_en: Artificial Narrow Intelligence systems appear intelligent but have no awareness of what they are doing (I-2). Artificial General Intelligence acts and thinks like a conscious, smart human (II-3). Super Intelligence goes beyond human intelligence (III-1). So the match is I-2, II-3, III-1.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Which among the following given below is correct in context of privacy issues in social media and online platforms?

options.en: The sharing on social media especially by children must be monitored at all times.
The addiction of social media does not hamper the academic performance of a student.
Rumours and fake news cannot put the administration at risk.
Mishandling of social media cannot create tension in the law and order.

questions.explanation_en: Children are especially at risk of privacy violations and cyberbullying, so what they share on social media should be monitored. The other options are false: social media addiction can hurt studies, and rumours, fake news and misuse of social media can disturb law and order.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Over half of the e-waste generated in the developed world are exported to developing countries, mainly to ______, where metals like copper, iron, silicon, nickel and gold are recovered during recycling process.
questions.explanation_en: Studies on e-waste report that a large share of the e-waste from developed countries is shipped to developing countries, with India (along with China and parts of Africa) a major destination. There, metals such as copper, iron, nickel and gold are recovered, often by unsafe informal recycling.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: IPR (Intellectual Property Right) is given for how much time, in digital realm?

options.en: Depending on case to case basis

questions.explanation_en: Intellectual property rights such as copyright, patents and designs, including those for digital works, are granted only for a limited, certain period. For example, a patent lasts 20 years and copyright lasts for the author's life plus 60 years in India. After that the work goes into the public domain, so the protection is not unlimited.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: The lowest cost solution to developing a KM system is:
questions.explanation_en: Per standard KM texts (Awad & Ghaziri), in-house development uses the organisation's existing IT staff, tools and knowledge of its own processes, so no vendor licence, consultancy or customisation fees are paid; this is treated as the lowest-cost route. An off-the-shelf solution looks cheap but adds licence cost plus the expense of adapting a generic product, while outsourcing pays an external firm's margin. End-user development is cheap to start but usually yields poorly integrated systems.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Marginal revenue is calculated by _____.

options.en: dividing the change in total output quantity by the change in total revenue
dividing the change in total cost by the change in total output quantity
dividing the change in total revenue by the change in total output quantity
dividing the change in total revenue by the change in total profit

questions.explanation_en: Marginal revenue is the additional revenue from selling one more unit: MR = ΔTR / ΔQ, i.e. change in total revenue divided by change in output quantity. Option 2 (ΔTC/ΔQ) is marginal cost, and option 1 is the inverted ratio.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Any account or goods used by the owner of the business for his personal use is called as:
questions.explanation_en: Cash or goods withdrawn by the proprietor for personal use are recorded as Drawings, which reduce the owner's capital. They are not business expenses, because they do not help earn revenue for the business.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following is NOT a type of business?
questions.explanation_en: In knowledge management, businesses are categorised by what drives their value: expert-driven, experience-driven and efficiency-driven businesses. 'Expense driven' is not one of these categories, so it is the odd one out.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following is NOT the purpose of knowledge management system?
questions.explanation_en: Knowledge management systems aim to drive strategy, integrate knowledge across the organisation, and enable sharing of knowledge to improve decisions and innovation. Portability is a software quality attribute (ability to run on different platforms), not a purpose of a KMS.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following inflations describes how demand for goods and services can drive up their prices?
questions.explanation_en: Demand-pull inflation occurs when aggregate demand exceeds supply, pulling prices up. Cost-push inflation is caused by rising input costs (wages, raw materials), and built-in inflation comes from wage-price expectations. 'Demand-push' is not a standard term.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Who is the father of e-commerce in India?
questions.explanation_en: K. Vaitheeswaran, co-founder of Fabmall/Indiaplaza (1999), is widely called the father of e-commerce in India. Michael Aldrich invented online shopping in the UK (1979), so he is the father of e-commerce globally, not of Indian e-commerce.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: An organisation structure establishes relationships between:
questions.explanation_en: An organisation structure defines authority and responsibility relationships among people, the work they do and the resources they use. The other options describe external relationships (environment, customers, society), which are not set by internal structure.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: _____ is a person who carries on business by himself/herself.
questions.explanation_en: A sole proprietorship is a business owned, managed and controlled by one person who bears all risks and profits. A partnership needs two or more persons and a cooperative is a voluntary association of members.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: The set of processes developed in an organisation to create, gather, store, transfer and apply knowledge best describes:
questions.explanation_en: Knowledge management is the set of processes to create, gather, store, transfer (share) and apply knowledge in an organisation. Organisational memory is only the stored knowledge, and a knowledge asset is the knowledge itself, not the processes.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following refers to focusing on determining, organising, directing, facilitating and monitoring knowledge-related practices and activities required to achieve the desired business strategies and objectives with reference to knowledge management in organisations?
questions.explanation_en: From the management point of view, KM focuses on determining, organising, directing, facilitating and monitoring knowledge-related practices to achieve business strategies. The business point of view is about why/where the organisation should invest in knowledge, and the hands-on operational view is about applying expertise in daily work.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: The demand is said to be ______ when a very insignificant change in price leads to an infinite change in quantity demanded.
questions.explanation_en: Demand is perfectly elastic (Ed = ∞) when a negligible change in price causes an infinite change in quantity demanded; the demand curve is horizontal. Perfectly inelastic (Ed = 0) is the opposite case where quantity does not change at all.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following is defined as that branch of economic analysis that studies the economic behaviour of the individual unit and may be a person, a particular household or a particular firm?
questions.explanation_en: Microeconomics studies the behaviour of individual units such as a consumer, household or firm. Macroeconomics studies the economy as a whole (national income, inflation, unemployment).

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Which step of the knowledge management process involves adding value by discovering relationships, abstracting and sharing?
questions.explanation_en: Knowledge refining adds value to captured knowledge by discovering relationships, abstracting, synthesising and sharing it. Gathering/acquisition only collects knowledge, and organisation only stores/structures it.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following is the proper sequence of the accounting cycle?

options.en: Recording of Transaction → Journal → Ledger → Trial Balance → Adjusted Trial Balance → Adjustment Entries → Closing Entries → Financial Statement
Recording of Transaction → Journal → Ledger → Trial Balance → Adjustment Entries → Adjusted Trial Balance → Closing Entries → Financial Statement
Recording of Transaction → Journal → Ledger → Trial Balance → Adjustment Entries → Closing Entries → Adjusted Trial Balance → Financial Statement
Recording of Transaction → Journal → Ledger → Trial Balance → Adjustment Entries → Adjusted Trial Balance → Financial Statement → Closing Entries

questions.explanation_en: Key doubt: the standard accounting cycle is Transactions → Journal → Ledger → Trial Balance → Adjustment Entries → Adjusted Trial Balance → Financial Statements → Closing Entries, which is option 4. Financial statements are prepared from the adjusted trial balance BEFORE closing entries, because closing entries reset revenue, expense and drawing accounts to zero. The official option 2 puts closing entries before financial statements, which is not the textbook order.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Interpretability, Format, Coherence and Compatibility refer to which quality of information with reference to Management Information System?
questions.explanation_en: In the Wang-Strong framework, representational quality covers interpretability, ease of understanding, format/concise representation, coherence/consistency and compatibility. Intrinsic quality covers accuracy and believability, contextual quality covers relevance and timeliness, and accessibility covers access and security.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following refers to the art of recoding, classifying and summarising in a significant manner, and in terms of money, transactions and events that are in part at least of a financial character, and interpreting the results thereof?
questions.explanation_en: This is the AICPA definition of accounting, which describes financial accounting: recording, classifying and summarising financial transactions in money terms and interpreting the results. Book keeping only records transactions and does not interpret results; cost and management accounting focus on internal cost control and decision making.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Activities like packing goods, loading goods and shipping goods belong to which step of the e-commerce primary process?
questions.explanation_en: Packing, loading and shipping goods to the customer happen in the delivery/fulfilment step of the e-commerce process. Contract conclusion is placing/accepting the order, billing is invoicing and payment, and service/support is after-sales.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: The ______ economic system is characterised by free markets and the absence of government intervention in the economy.
questions.explanation_en: A capitalist (free-market) economy is characterised by private ownership, free markets and little or no government intervention. A socialist economy has state ownership and planning, while a mixed economy combines both.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: With reference to stakeholders of e-commerce, business organisations abbreviated by ‘B’ may include ______.
questions.explanation_en: In B2B/B2C notation, 'B' stands for business organisations such as producers, manufacturers, wholesalers and retailers. Consumers/customers are 'C' and government is 'G'.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following refers to a planned system of collecting, storing and disseminating data in the form of information needed to carry out the functions of management?
questions.explanation_en: A Management Information System is a planned system for collecting, storing and disseminating data as information needed by managers to plan, organise and control. A DBMS only manages data storage and retrieval; it does not by itself serve management functions.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: The most common type of business organisation is:
questions.explanation_en: Sole proprietorship is the most common form of business organisation because it is easy to start, needs little capital and has few legal formalities. Partnerships and companies require more agreements and registration.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: ______ is also referred to as the Sales-Force-Composite method or the Collective Opinion Method.
questions.explanation_en: The opinion survey method includes the sales-force composite (collective opinion) method, where salespeople's estimates of expected sales are combined. The consumer interview method surveys buyers directly, and the evolutionary/substitute approaches are for new products.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: In a management information system, what is/are the formal social unit that is/are devoted to attaining specified goals?
questions.explanation_en: An organisation is a formal social unit (a group of people) deliberately structured to achieve specified goals. Management is the process of directing that unit, and marketing is one of its functions.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: The ______ E-commerce segment(s) is/are represented by OLX.
questions.explanation_en: OLX is a classifieds platform where individuals sell used goods directly to other individuals, so it is Consumer-to-Consumer (C2C). B2C examples are Amazon/Flipkart retail and B2B examples are IndiaMART.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following accounts is/are prepared for net profit?

options.en: Trading account, profit and loss account and balance sheet

questions.explanation_en: Net profit is found in the Profit and Loss Account, which deducts indirect expenses from gross profit. The Trading Account gives gross profit, and the Balance Sheet is a statement of assets and liabilities, not an account.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: A public company must have at least ______ members.
questions.explanation_en: Under the Companies Act, 2013, a public company needs at least 7 members (a private company needs 2, a One Person Company needs 1). Option 3 (2) is the minimum for a private company.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following business structures has limited liability to its members?
questions.explanation_en: A company is a separate legal entity, so its members' liability is limited to the unpaid amount on their shares. Sole proprietors and (general) partners have unlimited liability; a cooperative society may also have limited liability, but the company is the classic answer.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Which method is used for demand forecasting of new products?

options.en: Evolutionary approach, opinion polling approach and vicarious approach

questions.explanation_en: Joel Dean's methods for forecasting demand for new products include the evolutionary approach, substitute approach, opinion polling approach, growth-curve approach and vicarious approach. Since all three listed approaches are valid, option 1 (all of them) is correct; picking only one is incomplete.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: What is a long-term asset in accounting?
questions.explanation_en: Long-term assets are fixed (non-current) assets such as land, buildings and machinery, held for more than one year to run the business. Liabilities are obligations, not assets; intangible assets are one sub-type, while 'fixed assets' is the general term.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: What is the advantage of exploratory Data Analysis in Big Data and Analytics?

options.en: Usually does not provide definitive answers

questions.explanation_en: Exploratory Data Analysis is flexible and visual, letting analysts discover patterns and generate new hypotheses before formal modelling. Not giving definitive answers and less realistic statements of accuracy are drawbacks of EDA, not advantages.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en:
In AI biases many AI models are ______.
I. deepfakes
II. Black boxes
III. K-anonymity
questions.explanation_en: Many AI models, especially deep neural networks, are 'black boxes': their internal reasoning is hard to interpret, so hidden biases are difficult to detect. Deepfakes are AI-generated fake media and k-anonymity is a privacy technique, so only II is correct.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: In cyber security, what remedy does the law provide?
questions.explanation_en: Cyber laws such as the IT Act, 2000 provide legal remedies including penalties, compensation and imprisonment for cyber offences. Technologies and computer networks are tools, not legal remedies, and an apology is not a remedy provided by law.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: In context of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, which of the given following is correct?

options.en: “Child” means an individual who has not completed the age of eighteen years
“Digital personal data” means personal data in physical form
“Chairperson” does not mean the chairperson of the board

questions.explanation_en: Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, a 'child' is an individual who has not completed eighteen years of age. Digital personal data means personal data in digital form (not physical), and 'Chairperson' does refer to the Chairperson of the Data Protection Board.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: ______ enables the creator owner to earn recognition or financial benefit by using their creation or invention.
questions.explanation_en: Key doubt: the statement is the WIPO description of intellectual property rights - IP is protected by patents, copyright and trademarks, which 'enable people to earn recognition or financial benefit from what they invent or create'. Because it covers inventions as well as creations, option 3 (intellectual property right) is the correct general answer. Copyright protects only original creative works, not inventions (those are patented), so the official key is too narrow.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: From the challenges given below, which of the challenge does IoT adoption include?
questions.explanation_en: Security (and privacy) is a major challenge of IoT adoption, because many connected devices have weak authentication and are hard to patch. Deepfakes and black-box models are AI issues, and cloud storage is a supporting technology, not an IoT challenge.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Irreparable computer and other electronic goods are known as ______ in tech world.
questions.explanation_en: Discarded, unusable or irreparable computers, phones and other electronic goods are called electronic waste (e-waste). They contain hazardous materials such as lead and mercury and need special recycling.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en:
The E-waste (management) rules 2016 of India, recognizes two broad categories: IT and telecommunication equipment and consumer electrical and electronics including which of the following material?
I. Fluorescent
II. Mercury
questions.explanation_en: The E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2016 cover IT and telecom equipment and consumer electrical and electronics, and they also brought compact fluorescent lamps and other mercury-containing lamps under their scope. So both fluorescent and mercury items are included.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: In digital realm, which refers to the legal rights to protect invention or creation in intellectual property, are given to whom?
questions.explanation_en: Intellectual property rights are granted to the creator or inventor of the work, giving them exclusive rights over its use for a period of time. Employees, sellers or buyers get rights only if transferred by the creator.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: In E-waste management, from which factors, there comes the exposure variability in electronic waste?

options.en: Quantity of the Pollutants in air
Management processes of the air pollution

questions.explanation_en: Exposure to e-waste hazards varies mainly with the type of e-waste (what device and which toxic components, e.g. lead, mercury, cadmium), along with how it is processed. Air pollutant quantities and air-pollution management are outcomes rather than the source of variability, and medical waste is a separate category.

tests.title: Previous Year Questions — Teaching Methodology (DSSSB 2023–24)
tests.subject: Computer Science
tests.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
tests.category: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching Special

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: Who among the following is known as Lokhitwadi?
questions.explanation_en: Gopal Hari Deshmukh, the 19th-century Maharashtrian social reformer, wrote under the pen name 'Lokhitwadi' through his 'Shatapatre' letters on social reform. Hence option 2.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en:
For preparing a unit plan, which of the following procedure is followed?
I. Formation of proper units and sub-units if not prescribed in the syllabus.
II. Determination of methods of assessment.
questions.explanation_en: A unit plan involves organising content into suitable units and sub-units (when the syllabus does not give them) and deciding the methods of assessment/evaluation for the unit. Both steps are part of the procedure, so option 1.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: David Kolb's model of learning style is based on which type of learning?
questions.explanation_en: David Kolb's learning-style model rests on his Experiential Learning Theory, a four-stage cycle of concrete experience, reflective observation, abstract conceptualisation and active experimentation. Hence experiential learning.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: Inconsistency in the development of different type of conservation is called _____.
questions.explanation_en: Piaget used 'horizontal decalage' for the uneven acquisition of conservation tasks - a child conserves number first, then mass, weight and volume later, though the same logic applies. So option 1.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: Heuristic method of teaching science was introduced by_____.
questions.explanation_en: The heuristic (discovery) method, in which the learner finds things out for himself, was introduced by H. E. Armstrong. The word comes from Greek 'heurisko', meaning 'I find out'.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding vision of new-born babies?
I. Neonates can discriminate between stationary black and white stripe which is 1/8 of an inch wide
II. By three months babies can see stripes as narrow as 64th of an inch wide
questions.explanation_en: Developmental research (Fantz and others) shows newborns can discriminate black-and-white stripes about 1/8 inch wide, and visual acuity improves rapidly so that around three months infants detect much narrower stripes (about 1/64 inch). Thus both statements are treated as correct.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: In the context of Parenting, which of the following is correctly matched?

options.en: Clearly communicating parent – Child being less liked
Power assertive parents – Coercive tactics in peer used by child
Parents being harsh – Unattractive social behavior of child
Give and take relationship of parents – Children show same relationship with peer

questions.explanation_en: Children model the relationships they experience at home: when parents maintain a reciprocal, give-and-take relationship, children show similar cooperative relationships with peers. The other pairings are mismatched (e.g. clear communication leads to well-liked children).

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en:
Broca's area and wernicke's area are concerned with language. These are the areas of _____.
I. right hemisphere of brain.
II. left hemisphere of brain.
questions.explanation_en: Broca's area (speech production) and Wernicke's area (language comprehension) are located in the left cerebral hemisphere in most people. Hence only statement II is correct.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en:
Which of the following is NOT a Neo-Freudian Theory of Development?
I. Henry Stack Sullivan's Interpersonal Theory
II. Erik Erikson Theory of Psycho-social Development
questions.explanation_en: Neo-Freudians kept Freud's basic ideas but stressed social and cultural factors. Both Harry Stack Sullivan's interpersonal theory and Erik Erikson's psychosocial theory are neo-Freudian, so neither is 'not neo-Freudian' (option 3).

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en:
Participation in which of the following activities can enable the community to accept a teacher as one of them?
I. Problems of unhygienic conditions.
II. Problems of agriculture.
questions.explanation_en: A teacher who participates in solving the community's real problems - unhygienic conditions as well as agricultural problems - wins its trust and is accepted as one of them. Hence both I and II.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en:
Considering the benefits to children with disability, which of the following provisions of Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan is correct?
I. Stipend for girls with disabilities
II. Braille textbooks
questions.explanation_en: Under Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan's inclusive education component, children with special needs receive aids and appliances, Braille/large-print textbooks, and girls with disabilities are given stipends to support their schooling. Hence both are correct.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: Reinforcement strengthens the occurrence of the emitted behaviour in the students. Which of the following is the correct example of positive reinforcement?

options.en: Teacher detaining the student after class hours.

questions.explanation_en: Positive reinforcement adds a pleasant stimulus after a desired behaviour to increase its occurrence. Awarding high grades is a reward, while finding loopholes, detention and threats are punishments or aversive stimuli.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: Which of the following does not come under lower form of writing?
questions.explanation_en: Lower (controlled/guided) forms of writing include copying, dictation, picture composition and guided writing. Paragraph writing is treated as a higher form of composition requiring organisation of ideas, so per the official key it does not belong to the lower forms.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: Which of the following is NOT correct in regard of Piagetian perspective of play?

options.en: Play is not possible for child without toys
The play is something which transcends both culture and time
The play is something related to nature

questions.explanation_en: Piaget saw play as natural, biologically based and universal across cultures and ages, arising from assimilation. Children can play without toys (pretend and imaginative play), so the claim that play is impossible without toys is not correct.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en:
Which activity children’s do to expand their vocabulary?
I. Fast mapping
II. Sorting
questions.explanation_en: Fast mapping is the process by which children quickly connect a new word to its meaning after only one or two exposures, rapidly expanding vocabulary. Sorting is a classification skill, not a vocabulary-building process, so only I.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: In which method of learning by work, student themselves decide objective and prepare plan for an activity?
questions.explanation_en: In Kilpatrick's project method, students themselves purpose (set the objective), plan, execute and judge a purposeful activity, learning by doing. Hence the project method.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: The ‘Kesari’ newspaper was published in which language?
questions.explanation_en: 'Kesari' was started by Bal Gangadhar Tilak in 1881 in Marathi; its English counterpart was 'Mahratta'. Hence Marathi.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: According to the Indian Penal Code, an offence is not punishable for a child below ______ of age.
questions.explanation_en: Section 82 of the Indian Penal Code (doli incapax) states that nothing is an offence which is done by a child under seven years of age. Hence 7 years.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en:
Parent and family involvement decreases student’s ______.
I. Achievement
II. Success
questions.explanation_en: Research consistently shows that parent and family involvement increases students' achievement and success; it does not decrease them. So neither statement is correct.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en:
Read the following characteristics of one of the piaget’s stages of cognitive development given as A, B and C. Select the correct stage from the options.
A. Complete generality of thought.
B. Development of strong idealism.
C. Propositional thinking.
questions.explanation_en: Generality of thought, idealism and propositional (hypothetico-deductive) reasoning are characteristics of the formal operational stage (11+ years), when adolescents think abstractly.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: Which of the following ailments is NOT caused by obesity?
questions.explanation_en: Obesity is a risk factor for lifestyle disorders such as high blood pressure, diabetes and joint/orthopaedic problems. AIDS is caused by the HIV virus, not by obesity.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: When learning is meaning making, then students are the meaning makers. The learning process in this context is ________.
questions.explanation_en: When learners construct meaning themselves, the process is constructivist and student-centred; the teacher only facilitates. Hence option 1.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: Which of the following statement is NOT correctly matched?

options.en: Child with special need - should be seated near the board
Performing art - every child should have clear view of board
Group work - sitting arrangement should be in clump or clustered
Group discussion - teacher should have eye contact with every child

questions.explanation_en: Performing arts need open space where children can move and see one another, not a clear view of the board. The other pairings - CWSN seated near the board, clustered seating for group work, eye contact in discussion - are correct.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: Integrated child development service provides nutritious food for children who are ______.

options.en: Below age of six years and too young to go to school

questions.explanation_en: The Integrated Child Development Services scheme provides supplementary nutrition through anganwadis to children below six years (too young for school), and to pregnant and lactating mothers.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: Which of the following is the activity related to community services?

options.en: Collect picture about different musical instrument and dances
Collect information about handicrafts of different place
Participating in decoration at the time of events
Explore food habit and living style of the people of different state

questions.explanation_en: Helping with decoration during school or community events is a service activity contributing to the community. The other options are information-collection or project activities.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: Auditory and visual co-ordination system is present in child from ______.
questions.explanation_en: Newborns turn their eyes and head towards a sound source, showing that auditory-visual coordination is present from birth, though it becomes more refined over the following months.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: All of the given are the methods of Information and Communication Technology - based assessment except ______.
questions.explanation_en: Concept-map construction with software, multimedia program development and computer-based testing all use ICT. Writing a reflection journal on paper is a traditional, non-ICT method.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en:
Which of the following is correctly matched?
I. A child calling all four legged animals doggie – under-generalization
II. A child using word 'duck' for only his toy duck – over-generalizing
questions.explanation_en: Calling all four-legged animals 'doggie' is over-generalisation (overextension), while using 'duck' only for one's own toy duck is under-generalisation (underextension). Both pairs are wrongly matched, so neither is correct.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: The philosophy of inclusive education was added in District Primary Education Programme (DPEP) in ________ year.
questions.explanation_en: The District Primary Education Programme (launched 1994) added an Integrated Education for Disabled Children/inclusive education component in 1997. Hence 1997.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en:
The given statement is referring to which type of identity status in adolescents?
'Experimenting and actively searching for alternatives in their struggle to establish their identity.'
questions.explanation_en: In James Marcia's model, identity moratorium is the status of adolescents who are in crisis - actively exploring and experimenting with alternatives - but have not yet made commitments.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: Which of the following stage is used for child cognition development at the age from 2 years to 7 years?
questions.explanation_en: Piaget's pre-operational stage spans roughly 2 to 7 years, marked by symbolic thought, egocentrism and lack of conservation. Hence option 2.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: The Government of India adopted the National Policy for Empowerment of Women in ______.
questions.explanation_en: The Government of India adopted the National Policy for the Empowerment of Women in 2001, which was also declared the Year of Women's Empowerment.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en:
In which of the following approach Pedagogy indicate learning by doing based on engagement of students through different activities?
I. Teacher centered approach
II. Student centered approach
questions.explanation_en: Learning by doing through varied activities that actively engage learners is the hallmark of the student-centred (constructivist) approach. The teacher-centred approach relies mainly on lecture and transmission.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: Which of the following approach of Assessment for Learning is the assessment of classmates on the response and performance of the learner?
questions.explanation_en: Peer assessment is when classmates evaluate a learner's responses and performance, giving feedback to one another. Self-assessment is by the learner himself and teacher-led assessment is by the teacher.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: Which of the following language was included through the 71st constitutional amendment (1992) in 8th schedule of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation_en: The 71st Constitutional Amendment (1992) added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali to the Eighth Schedule. Boro was added later by the 92nd Amendment (2003), and Bengali and Gujarati were original languages.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en:
Art education is the area of learning that is based upon which of the following?
I. The visual, tangible art
II. The performing arts
questions.explanation_en: Art education covers both the visual/tangible arts (drawing, painting, sculpture, crafts) and the performing arts (music, dance, drama). Hence both I and II.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: In which of the following approach to learning and teaching, both the teacher and the students perform activities strictly confined to the prescribed contents/ textbooks in the subject being taught?
questions.explanation_en: In the subject-centred approach, teaching and learning activities are strictly confined to the prescribed content or textbook of the subject. Learner-centred approaches go beyond the textbook to learners' needs and experiences.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: Piaget divided which of the following domain of development into four stages: The Sensorimotor Stage, The Pre-Operational Stage, Concrete Operational Stage and The Formal Operational Stage?
questions.explanation_en: Piaget's four stages - sensorimotor, pre-operational, concrete operational and formal operational - describe cognitive (intellectual) development. Hence option 3.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en:
Match the following Classification Of Cognitive Disability (Mental Retardation) with their range of intelligence quotient (IQ).
Severity Levels | Range of IQ
I. Profound Mentally Retarded | 1. 20-34
II. Mild Mentally Retarded | 2. Below 20
III. Severe Mentally Retarded | 3. 50-75
questions.explanation_en: Standard IQ ranges are: mild about 50/55-70/75, moderate 35-49, severe 20-34 and profound below 20. So profound = below 20, mild = 50-75, severe = 20-34, giving I-2, II-3, III-1.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: In the types of Learning resources, the term ______ denotes a partially three-dimensional, full-size replica or scale model of a landscape typically showing historical events, nature scenes or cityscapes, for purposes of education or entertainment.
questions.explanation_en: A diorama is a three-dimensional full-size or scale model of a scene (historical event, nature or cityscape), often displayed in museums. Realia are real objects, and globes are spherical maps.
