questions.explanation_en: _self loads the linked document in the same browsing context (frame or tab) that holds the link, and it is the default when target is omitted. _blank opens a new tab or window, _parent uses the parent frame and _top replaces the whole window.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: What happens when a visitor clicks the link Write to us?

options.en: The browser downloads a file named principal@school.in
The page sends an e-mail at once without asking the user
The default e-mail program opens with the address filled in
The browser shows an error because mailto is not a scheme

questions.explanation_en: mailto: is a URL scheme that hands the address to the user's default e-mail client, which opens a new message with the To field filled in. Nothing is sent until the user writes and sends the mail.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: In HTML5, the <hr> element semantically represents:

options.en: a hidden row placed inside a table
a thematic break between paragraph-level sections
a hyperlink reference to another page
a heading of the lowest rank on the page

questions.explanation_en: <hr> is an empty element that marks a thematic break, such as a change of topic, and browsers draw it as a horizontal rule. Its old presentational attributes (size, width, align, noshade) are obsolete in HTML5 and replaced by CSS.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: In the old-style <body> tag, which attribute sets the colour a hyperlink shows at the moment it is being clicked (the active link)?
questions.explanation_en: ALINK gives the colour of an active link, i.e. while the mouse button is pressed on it. LINK sets the colour of unvisited links, VLINK of visited links and TEXT of normal body text; all are now replaced by CSS (a:active, a:link, a:visited).

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following should NOT be placed inside the <head> section of an HTML document?
questions.explanation_en: holds metadata about the page: , <meta>, <link>, <style>, <script> and <base>. A <p> paragraph is visible content and belongs in <body>.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: A page contains the line <!-- Revised by Admin on 5 May -->. What happens to this text?

options.en: It is shown in italics at the top of the page
It is not displayed, but anyone can read it in View Source
It is encrypted and removed from the page source
It appears as a tooltip when the page first loads

questions.explanation_en: Text between <!-- and --> is an HTML comment: the browser does not render it. It is still sent to the browser as part of the source, so it must never contain passwords or other secrets.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: Which tag gives a title to an HTML table and must be written immediately after the opening <table> tag?
questions.explanation_en: <caption> supplies the table's title and must be the first child of <table>; browsers show it above the table by default. <th> is a header cell, <thead> groups header rows and <title> names the whole page in <head>.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: A form contains <input type="email" name="mail" required>. The user types only abc and clicks Submit. What does a modern browser do?

options.en: It sends abc to the server without any check
It appends a default domain to the value and sends it
It clears the field and submits the form empty
It stops submission and asks for a valid e-mail address

questions.explanation_en: type="email" makes the browser check that the value looks like an e-mail address (it must contain @ and a domain part). Because the check fails, the form is not submitted and a validation message is shown. Server-side validation is still needed because client checks can be bypassed.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: A form lets students upload a photo using <input type="file" name="pic">. Which <form> settings are needed for the file contents to actually reach the server?
questions.explanation_en: File data travels in the request body, so the form must use POST; GET only appends name=value pairs to the URL. The enctype must be multipart/form-data, because the default application/x-www-form-urlencoded sends just the file name. application/json is not a valid enctype for an HTML form.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: An <h1> is styled by an external stylesheet (color: blue), by an internal <style> block placed after the <link> (color: green) and by its own inline style attribute (color: red). All rules use the same selector type and none uses !important. Which colour does the heading show?
questions.explanation_en: CSS can be added inline (style attribute), internally (<style> in the head) or externally (<link> to a .css file). An inline style has the highest priority, so red wins. Between internal and external rules of equal specificity, the one that comes later in the document wins.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: Which elements are selected by the CSS selector h2 + p?

options.en:
Every

that is nested inside an

Every

that comes anywhere after an

Only the

immediately after an

, with the same parent

All

elements together with all

elements

questions.explanation_en:
The + combinator is the adjacent-sibling selector: it matches a

that directly follows an

and shares its parent. h2 ~ p would match every later sibling

, h2 p matches descendants and h2, p is a group selector.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: In the CSS box model, which area lies outside the border and is always transparent, never showing the element's background colour?
questions.explanation_en: From inside out, the box model is content, padding, border and margin. Padding takes the element's background, but the margin is clear space outside the border that shows whatever lies behind the element.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies

options.en: The width jumps to 250px at once and resets after 2 seconds
The width grows smoothly from 100px to 250px over 2 seconds
The width waits 2 seconds and then jumps to 250px
Nothing changes, because a @keyframes rule is missing

questions.explanation_en: transition: width 2s tells the browser to animate any change in width over 2 seconds instead of applying it instantly. On hover the width moves gradually to 250px, and it moves back smoothly when the pointer leaves. @keyframes is needed only for CSS animations, not transitions.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en:
What is the visible effect of this rule?
```css
img { filter: blur(4px); }
```

options.en: All images appear out of focus (blurred)
All images get a 4px black border
All images are shown in greyscale
All images shrink by 4px on each side

questions.explanation_en: The CSS filter property applies graphic effects; blur(4px) applies a Gaussian blur whose radius (the standard deviation of the Gaussian) is 4px. Other filter functions include grayscale(), brightness(), contrast() and sepia().

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: In Sass (SCSS syntax), how is a variable holding the main theme colour declared?
questions.explanation_en: Sass variables begin with $, and the preprocessor compiles them into plain CSS. LESS uses the @ prefix, while native CSS custom properties are written as --primary: value; inside a rule and read with var(--primary).

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en:
What does the following rule do?
```css
.box { display: flex; justify-content: center; }
```

options.en: Centres the child items along the main (horizontal) axis
Centres only the text inside each child item
Stacks the child items vertically in the middle
Centres the .box element itself on the page

questions.explanation_en: display: flex makes .box a flex container whose children are laid out in a row by default. justify-content aligns those children along the main axis, so center groups them in the middle horizontally. Vertical alignment in a row is controlled by align-items.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies

options.en: 23A on line 1 and A23 on line 2
5A on line 1 and A5 on line 2
5A on line 1 and A23 on line 2
23A on line 1 and A5 on line 2

questions.explanation_en: The + operator works left to right. In 2 + 3 + "A" the numbers are added first (5) and then joined to "A", giving 5A. In "A" + 2 + 3 the first operation already involves a string, so 2 and 3 are joined as text, giving A23.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.explanation_en: var is function-scoped, so all three callbacks share one variable i. The callbacks run only after the loop finishes, when i is already 3, so 3 is printed three times. Declaring the loop variable with let creates a new binding per iteration and prints 0 1 2.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.explanation_en: a++ returns the old value 5 and then makes a = 6. ++a then increases a to 7 and returns 7. So b = 5 + 7 = 12, and a ends as 7.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en:
What is printed?
```javascript
console.log(Boolean(""), Boolean("0"));
```
questions.explanation_en: The empty string is one of JavaScript's falsy values, so Boolean("") is false. "0" is a non-empty string, and every non-empty string is truthy, so Boolean("0") is true.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en:
What is the output of the following statement?
```javascript
console.log(0.1 + 0.2 === 0.3);
```
questions.explanation_en: JavaScript stores numbers as 64-bit binary floating point, in which 0.1 and 0.2 cannot be represented exactly. Their sum is 0.30000000000000004, which is not strictly equal to 0.3, so false is printed.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en:
What does this code print?
```javascript
console.log([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6].filter(n => n % 2 === 0).map(n => n * n));
```
questions.explanation_en: filter keeps only the even numbers, giving [2, 4, 6]. map then squares each of them, giving [4, 16, 36]. Both methods return new arrays and leave the original unchanged.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.explanation_en: String indices start at 0, and slice(1, 3) returns characters from index 1 up to, but not including, index 3, which is "EL". The length property counts all five characters of DELHI.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: What does document.getElementsByClassName("note") return?

options.en: Only the first element having class note
null when more than one element has that class
A live HTMLCollection of all elements having class note
A static array holding the ids of those elements

questions.explanation_en: getElementsByClassName returns a live HTMLCollection of every matching element, which updates automatically when the document changes. It returns an empty collection, not null, when nothing matches. getElementById and querySelector are the methods that return a single element.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: Which JavaScript event fires when an input box loses focus, for example when the user presses Tab to move to the next field?
questions.explanation_en: The blur event fires when an element loses focus, and onblur is often used to validate a field as soon as the user leaves it. onfocus is its opposite, onload fires when the page finishes loading and onsubmit fires when a form is submitted.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en:
What does the following jQuery statement do?
```javascript
$("#banner").fadeTo("slow", 0.3);
```

options.en: Fades the element to 30% opacity and leaves it visible
Fades the element out completely within 0.3 seconds
Slides the element up until it is 30% of its height
Hides the element and then removes it from the DOM

questions.explanation_en: fadeTo(speed, opacity) animates the opacity of the selected elements to the given value, here 0.3, at the given speed. Unlike fadeOut(), it does not hide the element with display: none, so it stays on the page in a faded state.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: Which elements are selected by the jQuery selector $("p.intro")?

options.en:
The single

element whose id is intro
Every element with class intro inside a

The first

and every element with class intro

Every

element that has the class intro

questions.explanation_en:
jQuery uses CSS selector syntax, so p.intro means

elements carrying class="intro". An id would be written p#intro, a descendant would be written p .intro (with a space), and a group would use a comma.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: In AngularJS, which directive marks the root element of the application and automatically bootstraps (starts) AngularJS on the page?
questions.explanation_en: ng-app defines the root of an AngularJS application, and AngularJS starts automatically on the element carrying it. ng-init sets initial values, ng-model binds form controls to data and ng-controller attaches a controller to a part of the view.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en:
Inside a working AngularJS application, how many
  • elements appear in the rendered page for this markup? ```html
    • {{c}}
    ```

options.en: 3, one for each colour in the list

questions.explanation_en: ng-repeat clones its element once for every item in the collection, and {{c}} shows the current item. The array has three colours, so three <li> elements appear: Red, Green and Blue. The template itself is not displayed as an extra item.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: Which statement about XML element names is correct?

options.en: Names may begin with a digit, such as <1st>
Names may contain spaces, such as <first name>
Names starting with xml are reserved for users

questions.explanation_en: XML is case-sensitive, so <Student> and <student> are different element names and a start tag must match its end tag exactly. Names cannot start with a digit or contain spaces, and names beginning with xml (in any case) are reserved for the XML standards, not for users.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: An XML document is called valid when it:

options.en: opens without any error in a web browser
is well-formed and also obeys its DTD or XML Schema
contains only elements and no attributes at all

questions.explanation_en: A well-formed document follows XML syntax rules (one root, properly nested and closed tags, quoted attributes). A valid document is well-formed and also conforms to the structure declared in its DTD or XML Schema. Every valid document is well-formed, but not every well-formed document is valid.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: In the DTD declaration <!ELEMENT name (#PCDATA)>, what does #PCDATA mean the element may contain?

options.en: Parsed character data, i.e. text read by the parser
Character data that the parser ignores completely
Only other child elements and no text at all
Binary data such as images and sound files

questions.explanation_en: #PCDATA stands for parsed character data: text that the parser examines, so entities such as & are expanded and markup is recognised. CDATA sections, by contrast, are not parsed. An element declared only with (#PCDATA) holds text and no child elements.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: Why is a SAX parser usually preferred over a DOM parser for reading a very large XML file?

options.en: It builds the full tree in memory so any node can be changed
It can edit the document and save it back to the disk
It always validates against the DTD faster than DOM
It reads the file sequentially and raises events, with no full tree

questions.explanation_en: SAX (Simple API for XML) is event-based: it reads the document from start to end and calls handlers such as startElement and endElement, so memory use stays small. DOM loads the whole document into an in-memory tree, which allows random access and changes but needs much more memory for big files.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: According to the XML 1.0 specification, what must an XML processor do when it detects a well-formedness error, such as a missing end tag?

options.en: Report a fatal error and stop normal processing
Silently insert the missing end tag and continue
Skip the faulty element and display the rest
Convert the document to HTML and render it

questions.explanation_en: The XML processor (parser) reads the document and gives the application access to its content and structure. The specification treats a well-formedness violation as a fatal error: the processor must report it and must not continue normal processing. This strictness differs from HTML browsers, which try to repair faulty markup.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: In the servlet life cycle, which method does the container call only once, when the servlet is first loaded, to do one-time setup?
questions.explanation_en: The servlet container (for example Tomcat) loads the class, creates one instance and calls init() once. It then calls service() for every request, which passes the request to doGet() or doPost(). destroy() is called once when the servlet is taken out of service.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: What was the main performance drawback of classic CGI programs that led to technologies such as Java servlets?

options.en: They could be written only in the C language
A new process was started for every request
They were unable to read submitted form data
They could run only on the client's machine

questions.explanation_en: The Common Gateway Interface defines how a web server passes a request to an external program and returns its output. Classic CGI starts a fresh operating-system process for each request, which is slow and wastes memory under heavy load. Servlets avoid this by handling each request on a thread of one loaded instance.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: In ASP.NET Web Forms, the Page.IsPostBack property is true when:

options.en: the page is being loaded for the very first time
the page reloads because its own form was submitted
the visitor's browser has JavaScript switched off
the page is being redirected to some other page

questions.explanation_en: A postback happens when a Web Forms page sends its form data back to the same page, for example when a server-side Button raises its Click event. IsPostBack is false on the first request and true on postbacks, so code such as if (!IsPostBack) in Page_Load runs initialisation only once.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: Which ADO.NET object holds an in-memory copy of one or more tables and works in disconnected mode, without keeping the database connection open?
questions.explanation_en: A DataSet, filled by a DataAdapter, stores tables, rows and relations in memory and can be used after the connection is closed. A DataReader is connected, forward-only and read-only. Connection opens the link to the database and Command runs SQL statements.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: A developer wants to inspect a page's HTML elements and try out CSS changes live inside the browser while designing the layout. Which front-end tool is meant for this?
questions.explanation_en: Chrome DevTools is a set of front-end development tools built into the browser for inspecting the DOM, editing CSS live, debugging JavaScript and checking network activity. MySQL Workbench is a database design tool, Apache Tomcat is a back-end servlet container and Composer manages PHP (server-side) packages.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: In a three-tier web application, which tier contains the business logic, such as calculating a student's total marks and grade?
questions.explanation_en: Three-tier architecture separates presentation (user interface in the browser), application or business logic (on the web/application server) and data storage (on the database server). The middle tier receives requests, applies the rules and talks to the database.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: A web server returns HTTP status code 403. What does it mean?

options.en: The server understood the request but refuses access
The requested page does not exist on the server
The server crashed while handling the request
The page has moved permanently to a new URL

questions.explanation_en: 403 Forbidden means the server understood the request but will not authorise it, for example because the user lacks permission. A missing page gives 404, a server-side failure gives 500 and a permanent move gives 301.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: Which HTTP status code reports a general error on the server side, such as an unhandled exception in a PHP script?
questions.explanation_en: 500 Internal Server Error is the generic code for a failure on the server. Codes are grouped by class: 2xx success (200 OK), 3xx redirection (302 Found), 4xx client errors (400 Bad Request) and 5xx server errors.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: Booking a railway ticket and paying for it through an app on a smartphone is best described as:
questions.explanation_en: m-commerce (mobile commerce) is buying, selling or paying through handheld devices such as smartphones and tablets. It is a form of e-commerce; EDI is computer-to-computer exchange of business documents, and B2B is trade between businesses.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: A cookie is set with the Secure attribute. What is the effect?

options.en: It cannot be read by JavaScript on the page
It is deleted as soon as the browser closes
It is encrypted by the browser before storage
It is sent by the browser only over HTTPS connections

questions.explanation_en: The Secure attribute tells the browser to send the cookie only on encrypted HTTPS requests, so it cannot be read on plain HTTP traffic. Hiding a cookie from JavaScript is done by HttpOnly, and a cookie without Expires or Max-Age is a session cookie that ends when the browser closes.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Web Technologies
questions.question_en: The Content-Security-Policy (CSP) HTTP response header is mainly used to:

options.en: limit the sources allowed to supply scripts, reducing XSS
encrypt the cookies that are sent to the browser
compress the page so that it loads more quickly
block SQL injection inside database queries

questions.explanation_en: CSP lets a site declare which sources of scripts, styles, images and so on the browser may load, for example script-src 'self'. Injected inline or third-party scripts are then refused, which greatly reduces the impact of cross-site scripting. SQL injection is prevented on the server with parameterised queries.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Cells A1:A6 contain 45, 50, 72, the text "NA", 50 and 38. What does =COUNTIF(A1:A6,">=50") return?
questions.explanation_en: COUNTIF counts the cells that meet the condition. The numbers 50, 72 and 50 are greater than or equal to 50, so the result is 3. The text "NA" cannot satisfy a numeric comparison and is not counted.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: What does the formula =LEN(TRIM("  Delhi   Board  ")) return? (The text has 2 leading spaces, 3 spaces between the words and 2 trailing spaces.)
questions.explanation_en: Excel's TRIM removes leading and trailing spaces and reduces every run of spaces between words to a single space, giving "Delhi Board". LEN then counts 5 + 1 + 5 = 11 characters. Without TRIM the length would be 17.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: A1 contains 55 and B1 contains 38. What does =IF(AND(A1>=40,B1>=40),"Pass","Fail") return?
questions.explanation_en: AND returns TRUE only when every condition is true. B1>=40 is false (38), so AND gives FALSE and IF returns its third argument, "Fail". With OR instead of AND the result would have been "Pass".

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: What value does the Excel formula =MOD(-7,3) return?
questions.explanation_en: Excel computes MOD(n, d) as n - d*INT(n/d), so the result always takes the sign of the divisor. Here INT(-7/3) = INT(-2.33) = -3, and -7 - 3*(-3) = 2. Many programming languages that truncate towards zero would give -1 instead.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Cells A1:A4 contain 10, the text "abc", an empty cell and 20. What does =AVERAGE(A1:A4) return?
questions.explanation_en: When given a range, AVERAGE ignores cells containing text and empty cells, so it averages only 10 and 20. (10 + 20) / 2 = 15. AVERAGEA would treat the text as 0 and give a different result.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: What does the Excel formula =LEFT("INFORMATION",4)&RIGHT("SYSTEM",3) return?
questions.explanation_en: LEFT("INFORMATION",4) takes the first four characters, INFO, and RIGHT("SYSTEM",3) takes the last three, TEM. The & operator joins text, so the result is INFOTEM.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: What is the result of the Excel formula =POWER(2,5)+SQRT(81)?
questions.explanation_en: POWER(2,5) is 2 raised to the power 5, which is 32. SQRT(81) is the square root of 81, which is 9. 32 + 9 = 41.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: In MS Word, which keyboard shortcut opens the Insert Hyperlink dialog box for the selected text?
questions.explanation_en: Ctrl + K inserts or edits a hyperlink in Word, and the same shortcut works in Excel and PowerPoint. Ctrl + H opens Replace and Ctrl + L left-aligns the paragraph.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: In MS PowerPoint, with a slide selected in the thumbnail pane, what does pressing Ctrl + D do?
questions.explanation_en: In PowerPoint, Ctrl + D duplicates the selected slide (or the selected object on a slide) and places the copy right after it. Ctrl + M inserts a new blank slide, Delete removes a slide and F5 starts the show. In Word, Ctrl + D opens the Font dialog instead.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: An Excel workbook containing VBA macros must be saved in which format so that the macros are kept?
questions.explanation_en: .xlsm is the macro-enabled workbook format; the m stands for macro. The default .xlsx format cannot store macros, .xltx is a macro-free template and .csv keeps only plain text values of one sheet.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Which information system records the routine, day-to-day transactions of a business, such as billing, payroll and railway reservations?
questions.explanation_en: A Transaction Processing System (TPS) captures and processes the large volume of routine transactions at the operational level. Its data later feeds higher-level systems such as MIS, DSS and EIS.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Which system gives top management summarised, graphical information such as dashboards, drawn from internal and external data, for strategic decisions?
questions.explanation_en: An Executive Information System (also called Executive Support System) serves senior executives with easy-to-read summaries, trends and drill-down facilities. It combines internal company data with external data such as market and competitor information.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: A Decision Support System (DSS) is mainly designed to help managers with which type of decisions?

options.en: Only programmed decisions taken by clerks

questions.explanation_en: A DSS combines data, analytical models and an easy interface so that managers can explore problems that have no fixed procedure. Typical tools are what-if analysis, sensitivity analysis and goal seeking. Routine, structured decisions are handled by TPS and standard MIS reports.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Information used by first-line supervisors for daily control, such as today's attendance list or items to reorder, is classed as:
questions.explanation_en: Operational information is detailed, short-term and used for day-to-day control at the lowest management level. Tactical information supports middle managers in medium-term planning, and strategic information supports top management in long-term policy decisions.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: In the information-quality framework used in MIS, which category contains accuracy, objectivity, believability and reputation?
questions.explanation_en: Intrinsic quality means the information is good in itself: accurate, objective, believable and from a reputable source. Contextual quality covers relevance, timeliness and completeness for the task, representational quality covers interpretability and consistent format, and accessibility covers ease and security of access.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Which of the following is an example of EXPLICIT knowledge?

options.en: A senior teacher's knack for calming a noisy class
A mechanic's feel for a fault from an engine's sound
A chef's instinct for the right amount of spice

questions.explanation_en: Explicit knowledge is codified: it can be written, stored and shared through documents, manuals and databases. The other three are tacit knowledge, which is personal, experience-based and hard to put into words.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: In Nonaka and Takeuchi's SECI model, converting tacit knowledge into explicit form, for example an expert writing her know-how as a guide, is called:
questions.explanation_en: SECI describes four conversions: socialisation (tacit to tacit, by shared experience), externalisation (tacit to explicit), combination (explicit to explicit) and internalisation (explicit to tacit, by learning and practice). Writing down personal know-how is externalisation.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: In the knowledge management process, which step involves cataloguing, indexing, filtering and linking the captured knowledge so that it can be found later?
questions.explanation_en: The KM process runs gather (acquire), organise, refine and disseminate (share). Organising arranges knowledge by cataloguing, indexing, filtering and linking it. Refining then adds value by contextualising, discovering relationships and abstracting, and dissemination delivers it to users.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: The senior executive responsible for an organisation's knowledge management programme is usually called the:
questions.explanation_en: The Chief Knowledge Officer (CKO) leads the KM strategy: building a knowledge-sharing culture, setting up repositories and communities, and linking knowledge to business goals. The CIO is responsible for information technology and systems in general.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: A blogger earns a commission whenever a reader clicks her link and then buys a product on an online store. This revenue model is called:
questions.explanation_en: In the affiliate model a site earns a referral fee or a percentage of sales for sending customers to another business. Subscription charges a fixed periodic fee, advertising earns from displayed ads and the transaction-fee model charges for each deal processed.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: A music app offers basic listening free with advertisements but charges a monthly fee for an ad-free premium plan. Which revenue model does this follow?
questions.explanation_en: Freemium (free + premium) gives a basic service free to attract many users and earns from those who upgrade to paid features. Licensing charges for the right to use software or content, and the sales model earns by selling goods directly.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Who is credited with inventing online shopping in 1979 in the United Kingdom?
questions.explanation_en: In 1979 Michael Aldrich connected a modified domestic television to a real-time transaction-processing computer through a telephone line, creating the first online shopping system. Jeff Bezos founded Amazon in 1994, Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web, and K Vaitheeswaran is called the father of e-commerce in India.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Under the Companies Act, 2013, what is the minimum number of members needed to form a private limited company?
questions.explanation_en: Section 3 of the Companies Act, 2013 requires at least two persons for a private company and at least seven for a public company. A One Person Company can be formed by a single person, and a private company may have at most 200 members.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: In a Joint Hindu Family business, the senior member who manages the business and alone bears unlimited liability is called the:
questions.explanation_en: A Joint Hindu Family (HUF) business is run by the Karta, usually the eldest member, whose liability is unlimited. The other members, called co-parceners, have liability limited to their share in the family property.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: A firm has current assets of ₹8,50,000 and current liabilities of ₹3,20,000. What is its net working capital?
questions.explanation_en: Net working capital = current assets - current liabilities = ₹8,50,000 - ₹3,20,000 = ₹5,30,000. It is the money available for day-to-day operations such as buying raw material and paying wages.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: A business has total assets of ₹5,00,000 and outside liabilities of ₹1,80,000. According to the accounting equation, what is the owner's capital?
questions.explanation_en: The accounting equation is Assets = Liabilities + Capital, which follows from the dual-aspect (double entry) principle. So Capital = ₹5,00,000 - ₹1,80,000 = ₹3,20,000.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: The owner withdraws ₹10,000 cash from the business for personal use. What is the effect on the books of the business?
questions.explanation_en: Money or goods taken by the owner for personal use are drawings, recorded by debiting the Drawings account and crediting Cash. Drawings are not a business expense; they are deducted from the owner's capital in the balance sheet.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: In the accounting cycle, the trial balance is prepared from the balances of the:
questions.explanation_en: Transactions are first recorded in the journal and then posted to ledger accounts. The balances of all ledger accounts are listed in the trial balance to check arithmetical accuracy, after which adjustments are made and the final accounts are prepared.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: When the price of a pen rises by 10%, the quantity demanded falls by 25%. What is the price elasticity of demand (absolute value)?
questions.explanation_en: Price elasticity = percentage change in quantity demanded / percentage change in price = 25 / 10 = 2.5. Because it is greater than 1, demand for the pen is relatively elastic.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: The total utility from 1, 2, 3 and 4 cups of tea is 20, 35, 45 and 50 utils respectively. What is the marginal utility of the 3rd cup?
questions.explanation_en: Marginal utility is the extra total utility from one more unit: MU of the 3rd cup = 45 - 35 = 10. The MU values 20, 15, 10, 5 keep falling, which illustrates the law of diminishing marginal utility.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Inflation caused by a rise in production costs, such as higher wages or costlier raw materials, is called:
questions.explanation_en: In cost-push inflation, higher input costs push producers to raise prices even when demand has not grown. Demand-pull inflation arises when demand exceeds supply, and built-in inflation comes from expectations that keep wages and prices rising together.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Among Joel Dean's methods for forecasting demand for a new product, offering the product for sale in a sample market and using the results to estimate total demand is the:
questions.explanation_en: The sales experience approach test-markets the new product in a sample area and projects the result to the whole market. The evolutionary approach treats the product as an outgrowth of an existing one, the substitute approach treats it as a replacement for an existing product, and the vicarious approach studies consumer reactions indirectly through dealers.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Which section of the IT Act, 2000 punishes violation of privacy by intentionally capturing, publishing or transmitting the image of a private area of a person without consent?
questions.explanation_en: Section 66E (added in 2008) punishes this privacy violation with imprisonment up to three years, a fine up to ₹2 lakh, or both. Section 66C covers identity theft, Section 67 covers publishing obscene material electronically and Section 43 deals with compensation for damage to computer systems.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: What does Section 79 of the IT Act, 2000 provide?

options.en: Exemption from liability for intermediaries that observe due diligence
Punishment for cyber terrorism against the nation
Legal recognition of records kept in electronic form
The power to block public access to websites

questions.explanation_en: Section 79 is the safe-harbour clause: an intermediary such as a social-media platform or ISP is not liable for third-party content it only hosts or transmits, provided it observes due diligence and removes unlawful content on proper notice. Cyber terrorism is Section 66F, electronic records are recognised by Section 4 and blocking orders come under Section 69A.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, the person who alone or with others decides the purpose and means of processing personal data is called the:
questions.explanation_en: Section 2(i) of the DPDP Act defines the Data Fiduciary as the person who determines the purpose and means of processing. The Data Principal is the individual to whom the data relates, and a Data Processor processes data on behalf of a Data Fiduciary.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Under the DPDP Act, 2023, what is the maximum penalty for a Data Fiduciary's failure to take reasonable security safeguards to prevent a personal data breach?
questions.explanation_en: The Schedule to the Act sets up to ₹250 crore for failing to take reasonable security safeguards, the highest penalty in the Act. Penalties are imposed by the Data Protection Board of India after an inquiry. Failure to notify a breach or to meet children's-data obligations can attract up to ₹200 crore.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Under the Indian Copyright Act, 1957, how long does copyright last in a computer program (a literary work) published during the author's lifetime?
questions.explanation_en: Computer programs are protected as literary works, and Section 22 gives them copyright for the author's life plus 60 years, counted from the year after death. By contrast, a patent lasts 20 years and a trademark registration lasts 10 years at a time, renewable.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: The E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2016 made producers responsible for collecting their end-of-life products and sending them for recycling. What is this principle called?
questions.explanation_en: Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) makes manufacturers responsible for their products even after sale, including collection targets and channelling e-waste to authorised recyclers. The 2016 Rules covered IT and telecom equipment and consumer electrical and electronic goods, including CFL and other mercury lamps; they were replaced by the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022 from April 2023, which keep EPR.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: A voice assistant can set alarms and answer weather questions, but it cannot learn to drive a car. Which category of AI is it?
questions.explanation_en: Artificial Narrow Intelligence (weak AI) performs a specific set of tasks and cannot transfer its skill to unrelated tasks; all AI in use today is of this kind. AGI would match human ability across all tasks, and ASI would surpass human intelligence.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: A recruitment AI, trained mostly on past résumés of male employees, starts rating women candidates lower. What is the main cause of this bias?

options.en: Hosting the model on a cloud server
Too many layers in the neural network

questions.explanation_en: A machine-learning model learns patterns from its training data, so historical imbalance in the data is reproduced in its predictions. Such bias is often hard to spot because many models are black boxes; remedies include balanced data, fairness testing and explainable AI.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Smart devices from different manufacturers use different protocols and cannot work together in one home. Which IoT challenge does this show?
questions.explanation_en: Interoperability is the ability of devices and systems from different vendors to exchange data and work together, and the lack of common standards makes it a major IoT challenge. Other key challenges are security and privacy, power consumption and managing huge numbers of devices.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: A cloud infrastructure shared by several organisations with common needs, for example a group of state universities running one examination platform, is a:
questions.explanation_en: A community cloud is shared by a specific group of organisations with common concerns such as security or compliance, and its cost is shared among them. A public cloud is open to everyone, a private cloud serves one organisation and a hybrid cloud combines two or more models.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: Which 'V' of big data refers to the trustworthiness and accuracy of the data, for example fake reviews or faulty sensor readings?
questions.explanation_en: Veracity is about data quality and reliability: noise, bias and errors reduce it. Volume is the amount of data, velocity is the speed at which it arrives and variety is the range of formats; value is often added as the fifth V.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: The very first block of a blockchain, which has no previous block to refer to, is called the:
questions.explanation_en: The genesis block (block 0) starts the chain, and every later block stores the hash of the block before it. Bitcoin's genesis block was mined in January 2009. An orphan (strictly, stale) block is a valid block that ends up outside the main chain.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — IT Tools & Emerging Technologies
questions.question_en: SWAYAM, a Government of India platform launched in 2017, is mainly used for:

options.en: a locker for citizens' digital documents

questions.explanation_en: SWAYAM (Study Webs of Active-Learning for Young Aspiring Minds), run by the Ministry of Education, offers free MOOCs from school to postgraduate level, with optional paid certification exams. Digital documents are kept in DigiLocker and UPI payments run on NPCI's network.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: In R.H. Dave's classification of the psychomotor domain, the highest level, at which a skill such as touch-typing becomes automatic and natural, is:
questions.explanation_en: Dave's psychomotor levels run Imitation, Manipulation, Precision, Articulation and Naturalisation. At Naturalisation the skill is performed automatically with little conscious effort, so it is the highest level.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en:
Match the objective with its level in the revised Bloom's taxonomy.
A. State the full form of ALU
B. Explain in your own words why RAM is volatile
C. Use a for loop to print the table of 7
D. Design a new quiz app for the class
1. Apply   2. Create   3. Remember   4. Understand
questions.explanation_en: Stating a full form is recall (Remember) and explaining in one's own words is Understand. Using a loop in a new task is Apply, and designing an original product is Create.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: The Herbartian steps of lesson planning are based on which psychological idea?

options.en: Apperception - new ideas link to existing ideas
Insight - sudden grasp of the whole problem
Scaffolding - temporary adult support in learning

questions.explanation_en: Herbart held that new knowledge is learnt by linking it to the 'apperceptive mass' of ideas already in the mind. His four formal steps (clearness, association, system, method), later expanded by his followers Ziller and Rein into the five steps (preparation, presentation, association, generalisation, application), are built on this apperception theory.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: The RCEM approach to lesson planning, which states objectives as expected behavioural outcomes in terms of mental processes, was developed at:
questions.explanation_en: RCEM stands for Regional College of Education, Mysore, where this approach was developed. It refines Bloom's evaluation approach and writes objectives as mental processes such as knowledge, understanding, application and creativity.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en:
Which statement about the Herbartian approach to lesson planning is correct?
I. It gives more importance to the teacher's presentation than to pupils' activity.
II. Its five steps suit skill and appreciation lessons as well as knowledge lessons.
questions.explanation_en: The Herbartian plan is teacher-centred, with the teacher presenting and pupils mostly receiving. Its rigid steps work best for knowledge lessons and do not suit skill or appreciation lessons, so only statement I is correct.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: The correct sequence of the 5E instructional model based on constructivism is:
questions.explanation_en: The 5E model, developed by the BSCS team led by Rodger Bybee, runs Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate and Evaluate. Students first get interested and explore before the teacher formally explains the concept.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en:
Which statement about inductive and deductive methods of teaching is correct?
I. The inductive method is slower but lets students discover the rule and understand it better.
II. The deductive method moves from several examples to a general rule.
questions.explanation_en: The inductive method goes from examples to the rule (particular to general); it is time-consuming but builds understanding. The deductive method starts with the rule and applies it to examples, so statement II describes induction, not deduction.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: W.H. Kilpatrick classified projects into four types. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
questions.explanation_en: Kilpatrick's four types are producer, consumer, problem and drill (specific learning) projects. 'Evaluator project' is not part of his classification.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en:
Which of the following is correctly matched?
I. Cognitive constructivism - Jean Piaget
II. Social constructivism - Lev Vygotsky
questions.explanation_en: Piaget's cognitive constructivism says the individual builds knowledge through assimilation and accommodation. Vygotsky's social constructivism stresses that knowledge is built through social interaction and language, so both pairs are correct.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: In a school computer lab, items such as computers, printers and UPS units that are not used up in daily work are recorded in the:
questions.explanation_en: Permanent equipment that is not consumed in use is entered in the non-consumable or dead stock register. Items such as paper, cartridges and CDs that get used up go into the consumable stock register.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: A teacher firmly corrects one student who is chatting during a demonstration, and the students sitting nearby also stop talking. Kounin called this the:
questions.explanation_en: Jacob Kounin used 'ripple effect' for the way a correction aimed at one student spreads to others who see it. The halo, Hawthorne and Pygmalion effects describe rating bias, being observed and teacher expectation respectively.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en:
Which statement is correct?
I. Assessment of learning is mainly used to certify and report what students have achieved.
II. Assessment for learning is conducted only at the end of a term.
questions.explanation_en: Assessment of learning is summative and is used for grading, certification and reporting. Assessment for learning is formative and goes on throughout teaching to give feedback, so statement II is wrong.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: A test whose answer scripts get the same marks no matter which examiner scores them is said to have high:
questions.explanation_en: Objectivity means the score does not depend on the personal judgement of the examiner. Objective-type items and a clear marking scheme increase it.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: The split-half method and the Kuder-Richardson formulas are used to estimate a test's:
questions.explanation_en: Both methods measure internal consistency, which is one form of reliability. Test-retest and parallel-forms methods are other ways to find reliability.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: Under CBSE's CCE scheme, life skills, attitudes, values and participation in co-curricular activities were assessed as:
questions.explanation_en: CCE divided assessment into scholastic areas (subjects) and co-scholastic areas (life skills, attitudes, values, co-curricular activities). This made evaluation 'comprehensive', covering all sides of the learner.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: A computer-based test that picks the next question according to whether the candidate answered the previous one correctly is called:
questions.explanation_en: In computerised adaptive testing the software raises or lowers the difficulty of the next item based on the previous response. This measures ability accurately with fewer questions.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: Courses on SWAYAM are delivered in a four-quadrant format. Which of the following is NOT one of the four quadrants?
questions.explanation_en: SWAYAM's four quadrants are e-tutorial (video), e-content (reading material), self-assessment (quizzes and assignments) and a discussion forum. Face-to-face lectures are not part of this online format.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: A 5-year-old says a tall, thin glass has more juice than a short, wide glass, though both hold the same amount. He looks only at height and ignores width. Piaget called this:
questions.explanation_en: Centration is focusing on one feature of a situation while ignoring others, typical of the pre-operational stage. It is a main reason why such children fail conservation tasks.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en:
Match the theorist with the concept.
A. James Marcia
B. Diana Baumrind
C. Noam Chomsky
D. Lev Vygotsky
1. Parenting styles   2. Language Acquisition Device   3. Zone of proximal development   4. Identity statuses
questions.explanation_en: Marcia described four identity statuses of adolescents and Baumrind classified parenting styles. Chomsky proposed the inborn Language Acquisition Device, and Vygotsky gave the zone of proximal development.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en: A teacher announces that students who finish their lab programs correctly will not have to do the extra written homework. Removing the unwanted homework to increase the desired behaviour is an example of:
questions.explanation_en: Negative reinforcement increases a behaviour by removing an unpleasant stimulus. It is not punishment, because punishment aims to decrease a behaviour.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en:
Which statement is correct?
I. The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 recognises 21 types of specified disabilities.
II. Samagra Shiksha (2018) merged SSA, RMSA and Teacher Education into one scheme.
questions.explanation_en: The RPWD Act 2016 raised the number of recognised disabilities from 7 (PwD Act 1995) to 21. Samagra Shiksha, launched in 2018, combined Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan and Teacher Education.

questions.chapter: Fundamentals, SE, Web, IT & Teaching — Teaching Methodology of Computer Science
questions.question_en:
Match the commission or policy with its period.
A. University Education Commission (Radhakrishnan)
B. Secondary Education Commission (Mudaliar)
C. Education Commission (Kothari)
D. National Policy on Education (second NPE)
1. 1964-66   2. 1948-49   3. 1986   4. 1952-53
questions.explanation_en: The Radhakrishnan Commission sat in 1948-49 and the Mudaliar Commission in 1952-53. The Kothari Commission worked from 1964 to 1966, and the second National Policy on Education came in 1986 (the first NPE was in 1968).
